bullets.title: JPM raises SPX YE26 target to 7,800; market grinds through hawkish Fed overhang
bullets.body: JPMorgan lifted its S&P 500 year-end 2026 price target to 7,800 (from 7,600), citing ~10% consensus EPS upgrades to $350 for FY26 (+29% YoY) and $390 for FY27. Despite the constructive revision, equities closed mixed Wednesday as hawkish Fed rhetoric and inflation concerns beyond oil kept pressure on the tape; the market is still pricing ~33bp of rate hikes through year-end.

bullets.title: MU crushes Q3, guides Q4 to $50B revenue and 86% gross margin — +13% AH
bullets.body: Micron reported F3Q26 revenue of $41.46B vs. $35.9B consensus and EPS of $25.11 vs. $20.86, with gross margin of 84.9% (+310bps above consensus). F4Q guidance of $50B revenue, $31 EPS, and ~86% gross margin blew past Street by ~15%/20%; MU surged ~13% after hours. The company signed 16 strategic customer agreements (SCAs) covering 20% of DRAM and 33% of NAND volume through 2030, representing ~$100B in minimum cumulative revenue with take-or-pay structures — signaling supply tightness persisting beyond 2027.

bullets.title: AVGO unveils OpenAI 'Jalapeno' inference chip; QCOM announces Meta data center CPU deal
bullets.body: Broadcom received first silicon samples of its 'Jalapeno' chip for a frontier model leader (OpenAI), offering ~50% cost savings vs. typical AI GPUs with per-GW silicon content of ~$15/GW vs. $11/GW for TPUs; shipments expected to exceed 1.3GW. Separately, Qualcomm announced a multi-generation data center CPU collaboration with Meta (Dragonfly C1000), with production starting H2 2028, and raised its FY29 non-handset revenue target to $40B from $22B including $15B+ from data centers.

bullets.title: Oil below $70/bbl for 9th straight session; energy drags while rate-sensitive cyclicals lead
bullets.body: WTI crude fell ~3.4% to below $70/barrel, down ~35% from Iran conflict highs and at its lowest since before the conflict. Energy underperformed within the S&P while homebuilders, hotels/cruises, airlines, and fintech outperformed as rate-sensitive/high-beta plays benefited from a 6-9bp DM yield decline; 10-year Treasury hit its lowest level in over two months at ~4.40%.

bullets.title: Treasuries rally; 10yr tests 4.40% resistance — JPM sees 4.30% on sustained break
bullets.body: 10-year yields fell 8-9bps to ~4.40%, the lowest in over two months, with the 7-year sector appearing rich relative to Fed expectations, inflation, and growth metrics. JPM flags $44bn 7-year auction Thursday as a potential concession risk given stretched valuations; a sustained break of the 4.40-4.435% resistance zone targets 4.30-4.315%. Active core bond fund duration was sharply pared back in recent weeks.

bullets.title: Hawkish Warsh hardens dollar, ends 'debasement trade' — credibility hike risk if inflation stays hot
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh has printed more hawkish than markets anticipated, driving dollar appreciation broadly (more vs. majors than EM) and deflating inflation-hedge/debasement trades. If core PCE stays hot, analysts flag 2-3 credibility rate hikes could begin late 2025/early 2026, while Warsh's credibility faces scrutiny for reportedly mischaracterizing Phillips Curve dynamics and colleagues' views. Core PCE for May is forecast at +0.31% MoM, due shortly.

bullets.title: Goldman estimates $30B quarter-end equity selling at 95th percentile; momentum pair down 12% from highs
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs estimates ~$30B in US equity selling at month/quarter-end, at the 95th percentile vs. the early 2000s baseline. GS TMT Momentum pair pulled back ~12% from recent highs (described as a normal range), while the broader NDX managed +35bps on the day; small-cap outperformance vs. NDX was the largest 3-day stretch since 2024, with R2K up 21% YTD.

bullets.title: May new home sales miss badly at 580K vs. 640K expected — weakest since January 2026
bullets.body: May new home sales fell 7.3% MoM to 580K, the weakest print since January 2026 and well below the 640K consensus, with losses concentrated in the West and South. Prices rose +2.0% MoM but remain 8% below the October 2022 peak; architects' billings also slumped below 50 in May. Analysts expect recovery as crude prices fall and Iran-related uncertainty fades.

bullets.title: AI crowding at hedge funds is elevated; 2026 L/S returns already in double digits at half-year
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs flags elevated crowding risk in AI momentum trades driving hedge fund performance, with both Fundamental and Systematic L/S strategies carrying material momentum exposure. 2026 equity hedge fund performance is already in double digits at the half-year mark, raising questions about concentration and reversal risk.

bullets.title: GOOGL loses three high-profile AI researchers to Anthropic, including Nobel laureate John Jumper
bullets.body: Alphabet is set to lose Jonas Adler, Alexander Prtizel, and Nobel Prize winner John Jumper (AlphaFold co-creator) to Anthropic in the latest wave of AI talent departures from Google DeepMind. GOOGL shares fell ~2.45% in premarket on the news; the stock is also being added to the DJIA on 6/29, replacing VZ.

bullets.title: Data center backlash intensifies; 300+ bans/moratoriums threatening US buildout
bullets.body: Growing regulatory and public opposition to data center construction is emerging across the US — Virginia energy tax, Texas polling showing 56% opposition, and Duke rate hike being reduced. San Francisco office leasing from AI tenants hit ~$1.7B in 1H26 already approaching FY25 totals, but policy headwinds are rising for the broader buildout narrative.

bullets.title: Korea memory stocks forcing systematic EM selling; JPM raises KOSPI targets despite $95bn YTD outflows
bullets.body: Foreign investors have pulled a record $95B from Korean equities YTD (record for Asia), with over 90% from memory names as the stocks now breach EM mandate limits, forcing systematic selling on rallies. JPM remains constructive on the AI memory cycle and raises KOSPI targets to 12,500/15,000/8,000 (base/bull/bear), noting domestic retail has bought ~$80B YTD and government tax revenues from memory names over 3 years could exceed $350B.

bullets.title: AMZN Prime Day initial sales $8.3B, +5.3% YoY, beat $7.9B forecast
bullets.body: Amazon Prime Day opened with $8.3B in sales, +5.3% year-over-year, topping the $7.9B forecast, led by electronics, appliances, tools, and home/garden categories. The beat adds to evidence of resilient consumer discretionary spending even as casual dining (-18% YoY per Citi card data) and new home sales disappoint.

bullets.title: US lodging RevPAR surges +9.7% YoY; World Cup driving luxury and Vegas strength
bullets.body: Total US RevPAR accelerated to +9.7% YoY in the week ended 6/20, up from +7.1% despite 500bps harder comps. Luxury led at +17.3% YoY and Vegas Strip printed +30.2% YoY as World Cup-related hotel buyouts drove outsized demand; easier comps of 350bps arrive next week, suggesting momentum could continue.

bullets.title: BX Q2 realizations ~$500M, ~40% below consensus — triggers broad asset manager selloff
bullets.body: Blackstone disclosed Q2 realizations of ~$500M, roughly 40% below Street expectations, dragging the broader asset manager complex down 3.1% with alternative managers deepening losses. Investment banks/brokers also fell 2.4%; fintech and non-bank lenders were the offset with AFRM +8.1%.

bullets.title: Anthropic alleges Alibaba illicitly accessing Claude via fake accounts; escalated to US lawmakers
bullets.body: Anthropic sent a letter to US Senators and the White House alleging Alibaba is accessing its Claude AI model through fraudulent accounts, a significant escalation in AI IP enforcement with potential policy implications for US-China tech competition.

bullets.title: SMR and OKLO down 5-6%; hydrogen weak; electric utilities +1.1% on AI demand theme
bullets.body: Small modular reactor stocks SMR (-6.0%) and OKLO (-5.5%) declined alongside the hydrogen sector (BLDP -11.6%) while the broader S&P Electric Utilities Index gained 1.1%, supported by AI/data center electricity demand. Mizuho noted DOE's $17.5B nuclear loan commitment has no near-term impact on utility new plant development timelines.

bullets.title: JPM unwinds oil-hedged rates derivatives as crude/rates correlation breaks down
bullets.body: JPMorgan is closing oil-hedged rates derivative positions — including 10s/30s swap spread curve steepeners (taken off at +1.4bp profit) and stopping out of 2s/30s curve steepeners at -12.2bp loss — as swap spreads and implied volatility have decoupled from crude prices following the Iran MoU signing. The unwind reflects a regime shift in cross-asset correlations that previously tied oil to rates volatility.
